Class TaskManagerApplication

java.lang.Object
io.mcs.taskmanager.TaskManagerApplication
@SpringBootApplication public class TaskManagerApplication extends Object
Starts the Task Manager: the class Spring Boot is configured from, and the one the IDE and the Maven wrapper run. Not itself the JavaFX application: a main class extending Application refuses to start from a plain classpath, so this one hands over to DesktopApp, which brings up Spring and then the window.
Author:
Hamza Rasool, Abdullah Khan

    • acceptJavaFxOnTheClasspath

      private static void acceptJavaFxOnTheClasspath()
      Keeps JavaFX from warning, at every start, that its classes were loaded from the classpath rather than as modules. That is how Spring Boot, the Maven wrapper and the IDE all run it, and it works in full; the warning only says JavaFX's makers test the other way. The filter drops that one notice and nothing else: every other message of JavaFX's, its stylesheet warnings among them, still reaches the console.

    • smoothTextVertically

      private static void smoothTextVertically()
      Has JavaFX smooth text's tops and bottoms as well as its sides. By default it draws ClearType text smoothed only sideways, so at display scales such as 125% the rounded tops of large letters come out flat, as if cut off. It must be set before JavaFX starts, and a value given on the command line wins.

Task Manager: Software Construction, BESE-30, MCS NUST. Hamza Rasool and Abdullah Khan.
